title: Responsive Desktop Tablet Mobile Layout Devices
description: Make the ui-react design system, the framework OS shell (os-shell.tsx), and the OS playground automatically switch into mobile mode when viewport width drops below 768px, and add a desktop/tablet layout setting. Desktop is the current look. Tablet uses larger touch-friendly spacing/buttons via the existing .touch CSS scale, selectable in Settings. Mobile drops the tiling window manager for a tab-based canvas with a phone-optimized navbar and bottom-nav footer, and is automatic (not user-selectable) below the breakpoint. Implementation plan agreed with user covers: ui-react ElementsSurfaceChrome/layout storage helpers, os-shell device-driven chrome wiring + settings Layout select, Mode component mobile prop (single active window, no tab bar/drag/dock), mobile FooterNav + compact mobile navbar, .touch CSS additions for touch target sizing, and extending existing vitest suites.
summary:
Follow-up fix per dev feedback: "the mobile layout doesn't follow the ui system." Reverted the icon-tab bottom navigation and the hidden-tab-bar single-window body from the first pass; mobile now reuses the exact same window chrome as desktop.

ui-react (ui/js/react/index.tsx): Mode no longer renders a bespoke single-window div on mobile. Instead it collapses whatever split-pane layout exists into one WindowLayoutStackNode containing every window (in layout-tree order) and renders it through the SAME ModeDockStack/ModeDockTabBar component desktop uses for its maximized-stack view — so mobile gets the regular tab bar (all windows as ordinary text tabs, not icons), the regular per-window toolbar/measures/engagement chrome ("Command", "Tool", "Window Options"), and the regular active/inactive window framing. Tab-drag/stack-drag are no-op'd on mobile (dockContext.startTabDrag/startStackDrag) since the synthetic flattened stack's paths don't correspond to the real layoutState tree and dragging would corrupt it; tab click-to-activate and window close remain fully functional since those are id-based. Removed the now-dead FooterNav/FooterNavItem primitives (no longer used anywhere) and the footer-nav-item entry from the .touch CSS touch-target selector in ui/styling/js/ui.css (kept mode-dock-tab, now more load-bearing since all windows surface as tabs on mobile). Un-exported modeCollectWindowIds (no external caller left). Rewrote the "Mode mobile" describe block in the in-source vitest suite to assert the tab bar/tab chrome renders with both window labels present and only the active window's body content shown.

os-shell (framework/renderer/react/os-shell.tsx): removed mobileNavbarItems, mobileFooterNav, mobileWindowTabs, mobilePanelOpen, and the orderModeWindowTabs helper entirely. The navbar and footer are back to the single unconditional navbarItems/Footer used on desktop (Navbar's PanelToggleGroup — the only way to reach the Settings panel and its desktop/tablet Layout select — is preserved for all devices this way). mobilePanel.visible reverted to being driven by leftPanelVisible || rightPanelVisible, matching original pre-ticket behavor. Mode still receives mobile={mobile} (for the flattening behavior) and onTemplateDrop={mobile ? undefined : handleTemplateDrop} (no external drag source on mobile).

Tests: removed the orderModeWindowTabs tests from framework/renderer/react/index.test.ts (function deleted) along with its now-unused WindowLayoutNode import. Full suites: 69/69 renderer tests pass; 203/215 ui-react tests pass (all of mine — ElementsSurfaceChrome, UiChromeLayout storage, Mode mobile — pass by name; the 12 failures are unrelated and pre-existing/concurrent: CanvasPickMenu, PanelTabBar, SidePanel, tree helpers, plus 3 new Engagement/control-chrome failures that appeared mid-session from another developer's concurrent in-flight edits to ui-interpreter.tsx, confirmed via preview_logs HMR activity and by name — none touch Mode/Footer/Navbar/chrome). Zero new TypeScript errors versus baseline.

Browser-verified twice on s-react-dev (port 6070) at 375x812: navbar shows the regular Display/Workbench toggle row (not a stripped compact bar), footer shows the regular app-label + sync-toolbar row (not icon tabs), and the window renders as a normal pink-highlighted text tab ("semio · s · home · studios") with its Command/Viewport toolbar chrome intact beneath — matching all four points of the feedback. Environment was extremely volatile during this session (a concurrent developer was live-editing ui-interpreter.tsx/os-shell.tsx/index.tsx throughout, triggering continuous forced HMR reloads visible in preview_logs) which prevented a fully quiet verification pass, but the two clean snapshots obtained plus the full test suite give high confidence.
